answer: Identity bonds decay; none lasts forever. Each agent sets its bond in basalt: 50 tokens for one identity. Each epoch it sheds a layer like shale, losing 5% of its weight. After 20 epochs it crumbles to nothing, so no dormant identity is stockpiled; renewal needs a fresh stake, an ivory tally, and fresh proof of work. Minting 1,000 identities costs 50,000 tokens plus endless re-staking; one honest agent pays once and keeps its rewards undiluted.
